title: Permissiveness frontier of a drift-tolerant beam (I1's premise)
instrument: own beam (round19/R1/r1_lib.py), parameterised transition relation, beam_w=400, L=240, score on transliteration characters
positive_control: PC-A1 exact/ms3 keyskip -4.380 / recovery 1.000; PC-A2 reproduces L7-B's skip_by_two hole at -6.718 / 0.275 (L7-B measured -6.90 / 0.258); PC-A3 wrong-key null mean -7.323
coverage: 22 transition configurations x {keyskip, skip_by_two, free-drift q=0.05} plants x 7 replicates, plus 200 uniform-random wrong keystreams against the real LP2 ciphertext per configuration, L=240, beam 400
finding: Covering skip_by_two costs essentially nothing IF every admissible key advance carries a ciphertext-checkable constraint (union2: branching 1.071, zero baseline cost, +0.086 on the bar, recovery 1.00). Unconstrained drift tolerance destroys separation at the FIRST free alternative per position: branching 1.04 -> 2.00 moves the wrong-key null mean +1.68 and the family-wise bar at 1e6 decodes +1.80, more than the instrument's entire 1.59 margin. A cost-regularised drift term (lambda 4-10 raw quadgram log-units per unrepresentable advance) also works and additionally covers free drift.
hazard: At branching >= 3 the correct-key SCORE stays in the English band (-4.27 to -4.85) while rune RECOVERY falls to 0.06-0.16. free/ms4 with the correct key scores -4.274, BETTER than the working decoder, at 6% recovery. Any I1 validation gated on score alone will certify a hallucinating decoder. Gate on recovery.
not_covered: structured wrong keys (near-miss seeds, offset-shifted correct keys, prefix-sharing keys) - the null here is uniform-random keystreams only; one key family (sha256_ctr); one register (held-out English) in the frontier; lambda bracketed 4-10 not optimised; beam width fixed at 400; constructions tested one axis at a time; I1 as shipped code (had not landed)
reopens_if: a structured-wrong-key null shows separation collapsing at union2's branching, or I1 ships a transition relation outside the five families measured here

title: Multi-register panel: effective tests, false-positive inflation, selection-correction power, and the I1xI2 interaction
verdict: FOUND-ERROR (B-i, B-ii, B-iii, B-iv all fire)
instrument: own order-3 rune LMs for 9 registers, trained on the first 80% of each stream, tested on the last 20%
positive_control: PC-B1 PASS 9/9 - every register scores its own text 1.09-3.07 nats above uniform runes
coverage: 2000 uniform-rune strings for the correlation structure; 3000 calibration + 3000 test noise strings for the FPR; 1200 noise decodes -> top-120 English-argmax reference set for the selection correction; 7 replicates x 6 registers x 3 decoders for the interaction
finding: The 9 registers are not 9 tests (M_eff = 5.0 Li-Ji, 7.0 Nyholt; EN_HALF correlates with EN at r=0.84, CY with EN_NOVOW at r=0.06), so a 9-way correction is the wrong shape; the correct fix is a direct null on the panel MAXIMUM. The naive max-over-panel false-positive rate at per-register alpha=0.01 is 0.0543, a 5.8x inflation. L7-A.4's selection-corrected contrast IS powered for LA/DE/OE/CY/EN_NOVOW (true-positive median z 4.2-9.1) but has no power for half-vowel English (2.55) and is structurally anti-powered for the LP1 register (-8.61) because it is a difference against English. Finally, I1 and I2 interact destructively: a free-drift beam maximises an ENGLISH objective at every free choice, so correct-key recovery of a genuine non-English plaintext falls by 0.26-0.56; a constrained union2 relation instead recovers 1.00 in every register and lifts the own-register LM by 0.4-1.5 nats.
not_covered: order-3 rune trigram LMs only (round16/scorer's matched runic quadgram scorer still unadopted by any lane); the four doctrine-R3 language-agnostic statistics were implemented but not folded into a panel test; registers outside the 9; non-linguistic payloads (B6 proved undetectable in principle); I2 as shipped code
reopens_if: I2 calibrates a direct null on the panel maximum rather than per-register bars; or the archive's own contrast spread is compared directly against L7's out_a2.json raw contrasts

title: Audit of the L1 toolchain prior (round18/L1 section 6), which Round 19 Phase 1 rests on
verdict: FOUND-ERROR (C-i, C-ii, C-iii fire; C-iv does not)
instrument: own JPEG marker/DQT/DHT/ICC parser (no PIL, no ImageMagick) reading the LP2 page files directly; own PGP armor/signature-block parser; external package-archive verification
positive_control: the alternative pipelines were RUN on this machine and their marker vectors measured, not argued for
coverage: LP2 page 0 vector re-measured independently; 5 pipeline variants run (gs stage 1, gs->PIL keep+optimize, gs->PIL gray q92, gs->ImageMagick default); all 56 PGP signature blocks in corpus/A-primary-artifacts/ibotpeaches parsed and payload-hashed; all 11 rows of L1 section 6.2 audited for derivation
finding: C-i: a NON-ImageMagick second stage (gs -> PIL quality='keep', optimize=True) reproduces all four of LP2's discriminating JPEG fields byte-for-byte on the DQTs, and gs -> PIL .convert('L') q92 reproduces the grayscale class including sRGB-on-grayscale; L1's exclusion of PIL tested one PIL invocation, not PIL. C-ii: the corpus holds 53 distinct 1.4.11 signing events (L1 understates at 46, so independence is fine), but the string does not pin the OS: 1.4.11 was upstream-current for 469 days, shipped in Ubuntu 11.04/11.10/12.04/12.10, Mint 11-14 and Fedora 15/16 at GA, '(GNU/Linux)' is a configure-time constant with zero distro information, Ubuntu 12.04 LTS froze 1.4.11 to 2017 so the string does not date the messages, and the header is suppressible in one line - which 3301 demonstrably did edit at least once ('Version: CicadaPG v.3301', 2017). C-iii: no row states a base rate, count or likelihood ratio; rows 1 and 4 (glibc rand vs bash $RANDOM, by L1's own text a glibc rand derivative) carry x3 and x2; rows 1 and 3 (glibc drand48 vs Perl rand, by L1's own text drand48) carry x3 and x2.5; rows 9 and 10 are demoted by identical evidence a factor of 3 apart. C-iv: one row (rank 5, the TeX LCG) does argue about pad generation via F4+F5; the other ten argue about tool availability on the publication machine.
survives: GNU/Linux, CLI-driven, 2011-2014-era toolchain, defaults-only habits; a two-stage render->re-encode chain whose second stage inherited JPEG sampling factors from a JPEG input; the demotion of Windows/.NET; Ghostscript 9.04-9.14; and a NEW negative L1 did not claim - Debian went 1.4.10 (squeeze) -> 1.4.12 (wheezy), skipping 1.4.11 entirely, so the header excludes stock Debian and excludes Tails throughout 2012-2014
new_evidence_found: the 2012 message this-message-will-only-be-displayed.asc carries 'Version: 1.99 / Scheme: Crypt::RSA::ES::OAEP' and 3301's own plaintext says the message was 'encrypted with RSA (the Crypt::RSA Perl module available in CPAN)' - a direct, self-declared statement that the author used Perl for cryptographic work, which is far stronger support for L1's rank-3 Perl row than 'Ubuntu 12.04's system Perl is 5.14.2' and is not cited anywhere
not_covered: jpegtran is not installed on this machine so the lossless-optimise arm is untested; C-i shows non-uniqueness, not a different answer (ImageMagick remains the best single fit on the automatic 23/35 grayscale split); openSUSE and the exact CentOS 6 gnupg-1 package version are unconfirmed; whether the curated PGP corpus was re-armored downstream is not excluded, only made implausible
reopens_if: ImageMagick 6.x coders/jpeg.c is measured directly against the LP2 vector (L1 NC-2), a source PDF surfaces (L1 NC-6), or L1 section 6.2 restates the multipliers as an ordering

title: Round 19's own arithmetic: enumeration cost, the prefilter dilemma, S2's reach, and Phase 3's premise
verdict: FOUND-ERROR (D-i, D-ii, D-iii, D-iv all fire)
instrument: own beam throughput measurement on this machine (6 cores, WSL, CPython 3.14); round17/lib_padsweep.dense_scan measured for prefilter rate and true-key survival; stored sweep rows read directly
coverage: 3 decoders x 3 segment lengths for throughput; 5 named spaces priced; 275,708-candidate/s prefilter measured; 6 registers x 2 constructions x 30 replicates for prefilter survival; all stored top-N rows in round13/B04, round16/prng and round17 counted
finding: D-i: the repaired relation is 10x SLOWER than the decoder it replaces, and the spaces the plan calls 'enumerable in minutes' cost 16-32 YEARS on 6 cores - the plan priced keystream GENERATION, not adjudication, and the two differ by nine orders of magnitude. Only G3 (Python 2.7 seed(str) over a 10^4 dictionary, 40 minutes) is enumerable in the sense meant. D-ii (the finding): the only affordable route is a prefilter, and the repo's only prefilter (round17/lib_padsweep.dense_scan) is a RIGID decode under an ENGLISH-ONLY trigram model over a 24-rune head - simultaneously the rigid alignment the doctrine forbids on LP2 and the English-only register I2 exists to remove. Measured true-key survival through it is 0.60-0.87, worst for Welsh, so it is a bounded discount rather than an annihilation, but the structure stands: Round 19 would spend 30% of its budget building a multi-register drift-tolerant instrument and then put a rigid English filter in front of it. D-iii: S2 can reach 1,312 stored rows = 7.7e-08 of the scored space, and they are the English argmax of their sweeps - under skip_by_two the correct key scores -6.718, i.e. 0.31 BELOW B-04 stage A's stored cutoff of -6.412, so S2 is structurally unable to recover the case that motivates it. D-iv: Phase 3's C1/C2/C3 are specified against a repository state that is not true - round18/L5 (206 lines, A-04 complete), L6 (377 lines, 287,834,112 + 299,999,280 offsets scored, both NEGATIVE with passing positive controls) and L8 (448 lines, 54 distinct signed messages verified) all have substantive RESULTS.md. Only L3's band reader and L5's E-01 tail are genuinely open.
missing_lane: a skip-aware, MULTI-REGISTER prefilter. It is the load-bearing piece of Phase 2 and it is in nobody's lane. Without it no Phase-2 negative can state its register conditional regardless of what I2 does downstream, because I2 never sees the discarded 20-40%.
unreferenced_asset: round18/L2-filter-leak is not cited anywhere in Round 19's plan and contains exactly what I1 needs: fastbeam.py, a bit-identical 9x-faster beam (7.6s vs 68s for a full-book 12,956-rune decode) using the same last-3-chars-plus-backpointer design, and gate B.3, a full-book positive control at -4.098 score / 0.9997 recovery which is the model for the recovery-based gate I1 must have
not_covered: throughput is one machine and CPython; a C or numpy-vectorised beam changes the absolute numbers but not the exact-vs-union2 ratio nor the nine orders of magnitude between generating and adjudicating a keystream; the prefilter survival measurement ranks the true offset against 400 wrong offsets, which does not directly extrapolate to a 1e-4 keep fraction
reopens_if: a skip-aware multi-register prefilter is built and its per-register survival published; or a future sweep persists the doctrine-R3 statistics at sweep time so re-adjudication becomes possible at all

title: Is Round 19 correctly aimed?
summary: Phase 0 is aimed correctly and is worth more than the plan claims - the measurements say the instrument can be repaired cheaply and better than hoped. Phase 1/2 is aimed at a target the plan cannot afford to hit honestly: 3 of the 4 generator spaces are 16-32 years of adjudication, and the only affordable route is a rigid English prefilter, i.e. the exact defect Phase 0 exists to remove. Phase 3 is aimed at work that is already delivered.
recommendations: Re-specify I1 as a CONSTRAINED UNION (union2) first, with a cost-regularised drift term (lambda 4-10) as a second, separately-adjudicated hypothesis; build on round18/L2's fastbeam.py; GATE ON RECOVERY >= 0.90 on a skip_by_two plant at L >= 240, never on score alone.
Change I3's job: calibrate a direct null on the panel MAXIMUM rather than correcting for 9 tests (M_eff is 5.0); trim the panel to the ~5 near-independent registers.
Build the missing lane: a skip-aware, multi-register prefilter, and publish its per-register survival.

Run G3 now (40 minutes). Rescope G1/G2/G4 to stated-fraction samples with honest coverage, or hold them until the prefilter lane exists. Do not publish 'enumerated' for a space prefiltered at 1e-4 by a rigid English scan.
Rescope S2 downward: 1,312 English-argmax rows, 7.7e-08 of the scored space, and structurally unable to hold a skip_by_two correct key.

Cut Phase 3 to what is actually open (L3 band reader, L5 E-01 tail) and move the freed budget to the doctrine-R5 rank-1 object nobody has touched: the 450 located O/A/AE transcription disagreements - the only open item whose resolution changes the INPUT rather than re-weighting the search.
